topic: Matched minimax rate for CATE upper-level-set (optimal-subgroup) estimation in the super-margin regime xi*gamma > d, under the weighted symmetric-difference risk d_H(Ghat,G) = integral over Ghat symmetric-difference G of |tau(x)-theta| f(x) dx: over the law-level Holder/margin class (compact X with two-sided-bounded density, bounded Y, strict overlap, tau locally Holder-gamma on the near-threshold band and Holder-gamma' off it, pi Holder-alpha, mu_0 Holder-beta, margin exponent xi), prove that the minimax risk over ALL measurable set estimators is of exact order r_n*^(1+xi) throughout xi*gamma > d and in BOTH branches of r_n*, i.e. that Bonvini-Kennedy-Keele's Corollary 1 is rate-sharp on the regime their Theorem 1 leaves open and that the restriction xi*gamma <= d is an artifact of their construction; include the well-posedness half, that the tight-margin super-margin class is nonempty with tau crossing theta in the interior. The converse construction, the least-favorable family, and the transfer of achievability to the law-level class are delegated to the solve.

open_problems.open_problem: For an interior-threshold-crossing CATE on a compact d-dimensional support with density bounded below, what is the exact compatibility frontier between Hölder exponent gamma and tight margin exponent xi, and which part of xi*gamma>d is nonempty?

source_refs.claim: Proposition 3.4 shows that an interior threshold crossing is impossible when xi*min(1,gamma)>1, sharply constraining which nominal super-margin classes are nontrivial.
source_refs.author: Jean-Yves Audibert and Alexandre B. Tsybakov

source_refs.excerpt: Repair the nonseparated witness by requiring α_j<1/s_j ... or ... explicit smooth bump ... and reprove nonemptiness.
AudibertTsybakov2007 supplies the Hölder-margin geometry, but not this full-data compatibility audit.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The paper-side geometry and the prior-proposal failure point in the same direction: a nominal exponent inequality does not guarantee a nonempty crossing class. Audibert–Tsybakov rules out xi*min(1,gamma)>1, so most of xi*gamma>d is incompatible with an interior crossing under strong density; the viable smooth transverse case xi=1, gamma>d still needs an explicit observational-law witness satisfying bounded outcomes, strict overlap, and the separate nuisance Hölder restrictions. The secondary obstacle is therefore law-level causal embedding, not merely drawing a smooth contrast.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if nonemptiness theorem with explicit interior-crossing observational-law witnesses in every feasible exponent regime and an impossibility proof in every infeasible regime.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from margin-accelerated plug-in risk to the geometric restrictions behind super-fast regimes.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: margin converts regression error into fast decision risk -> smoothness can formally yield super-fast exponents -> interior crossing plus strong density restricts feasible exponent pairs -> characterize the nonempty causal super-margin class

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt Proposition 3.4's local crossing-volume argument and its explicit smooth regression constructions, then embed the contrast into bounded causal outcome laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves the structurally identical Hölder–margin compatibility restriction at a classification threshold, exactly the geometry needed by the requested nonemptiness frontier.

open_problems.open_problem: What minimal designated-version and regularity conditions make a CATE upper-level set and its weighted symmetric-difference risk well-defined functionals of the observed law while preserving the intended local minimax experiment?

source_refs.excerpt: The at-a-point target tau_P(x0) ... is NOT well-defined ... without an explicit version/regularity condition
Restate the target as ... theta_h(P), or add ... continuity or a Lebesgue-point condition at x0

open_problems.why_unsolved: Conditional means are equivalence classes modulo covariate-null sets, so a literal pointwise crossing statement is not automatically a functional of the observed law. Weighted symmetric-difference risk is invariant to null-set changes once the set is defined only modulo P_X, but interior crossing, Hölder membership, and the least-favorable perturbations require a common designated continuous version. The archived pointwise-CATE run identified this defect but did not prove that the repaired law-level class carries the same two-branch minimax experiment.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A law-level well-posedness and transfer theorem specifying a canonical CATE version, proving invariance of the weighted set risk, and embedding both minimax-rate branches into the repaired observational-law class.

writing_exemplar.why: Its smooth observational-law formulation is the closest template for explaining why CATE regularity is part of the statistical model rather than decoration.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CATE is only identified almost everywhere -> Hölder regularity selects a recoverable continuous version -> level-set geometry depends on that version -> transfer the minimax experiment to a law-level set target

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse the bounded observational-law embedding and localized fuzzy-hypothesis perturbations while tracking the designated continuous CATE version.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its lower experiment already coordinates propensity, outcome regression, and CATE smoothness; the missing step is preservation of the threshold-set functional.

method_exemplars.technique: Port the plug-in CATE-to-level-set risk inequality and verify it on equivalence classes of sets under P_X.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It uses the exact weighted symmetric-difference loss and supplies the achievability map that the law-level repair must preserve.

open_problems.open_problem: Is the minimax weighted symmetric-difference risk over all measurable CATE upper-level-set estimators exactly of order (r_n*)^(1+xi) in the feasible super-margin regime xi*gamma>d, in both nuisance-smoothness branches of r_n*?

source_refs.claim: Corollary 1 gives the plug-in upper rate, while the paper's minimax lower theorem imposes xi*gamma<=d, leaving sharpness outside that construction regime unresolved.
source_refs.author: Matteo Bonvini, Edward H. Kennedy, and Luke J. Keele

source_refs.claim: The paper proves the two-branch Hölder CATE minimax rate using localized fuzzy hypotheses, but it does not establish the induced level-set minimax converse under a margin condition.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, and Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: The classification analogue attains and lower-bounds super-fast plug-in excess-risk rates, but its binary-regression experiment does not automatically preserve observational causal nuisance smoothness.
source_refs.author: Jean-Yves Audibert and Alexandre B. Tsybakov

open_problems.why_unsolved: Bonvini–Kennedy–Keele's achievability follows by thresholding a sharp CATE estimator and applying the margin transform, but their lower construction is geometrically calibrated only when xi*gamma<=d. In the feasible crossing portion of xi*gamma>d, a converse must simultaneously create enough weighted set separation, keep n-sample affinity bounded, preserve the tight margin law, and realize whichever of the regression-driven and functional/nuisance-driven branches of r_n* is slower. Audibert–Tsybakov supplies the decision-theoretic analogy and Kennedy et al. supplies the two CATE lower experiments, but neither performs this joint causal level-set calibration.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A pair of least-favorable observational-law families, one for each branch of r_n*, yielding an all-measurable-estimator lower bound c(r_n*)^(1+xi) matched by the plug-in upper bound on every feasible super-margin exponent pair.

writing_exemplar.why: Adopt its direct arc from clinically meaningful CATE threshold groups to weighted set loss and minimax optimality, then pivot at the lower-bound regime restriction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CATE thresholds define optimal treatment subgroups -> plug-in CATE estimators induce weighted set estimators -> margins accelerate set risk -> determine whether the advertised rate is minimax sharp in the feasible super-margin regime

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the localized fuzzy-hypothesis construction that combines nonparametric-regression and quadratic-functional perturbations, separately activating the two branches of r_n*.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested rate r_n* is inherited from this exact two-branch CATE minimax experiment; the new proof must add margin-calibrated sign changes and set-loss separation.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the Assouad-style packing of threshold-sign perturbations and the conversion from regression amplitude and margin mass to excess decision risk.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Weighted CATE set loss is the causal analogue of classification excess risk, so its packing geometry directly targets the required (1+xi) exponent.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the higher-order local-polynomial CATE estimator, threshold it, and apply the paper's exponential-tail-to-margin risk integration argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the existing estimator and upper-bound proof whose rate the new converse must match without changing the target or loss.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct honest confidence regions for a CATE upper-level set whose weighted diameter adapts to the margin exponent, including the feasible super-margin regime and both nuisance-smoothness branches?

source_refs.claim: The discussion explicitly leaves the estimator's distribution and L-infinity theory for inference as important future work.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, and Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: The paper develops uniform inference for GATES selected by generic machine learning, not confidence regions for the spatial CATE threshold set under observational nuisance estimation.
source_refs.author: Michael Lingzhi Li and Kosuke Imai

source_refs.claim: The paper gives generic plug-in confidence regions for function level sets via local suprema, but treats density/function estimation rather than doubly robust CATE estimation.
source_refs.author: Enno Mammen and Wolfgang Polonik

open_problems.why_unsolved: Risk-optimal set estimation does not by itself provide coverage. A confidence region must control a supremum of a bias-corrected CATE process on a random shrinking near-threshold band, while accounting for cross-fitted propensity and outcome-regression errors and for the nonregular set map at tau=theta. Existing subgroup bands target sorted group averages, and generic level-set bootstrap theory lacks the orthogonal causal first stage and the two-branch CATE bias structure; adapting diameter to xi adds a further honesty-versus-adaptation obstacle.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computable inner/outer confidence-region construction with uniform coverage over the law class and a matching minimax theorem for its expected weighted diameter in each feasible margin and nuisance-smoothness regime.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its practical arc from noisy ML-selected beneficiaries to simultaneous guarantees, while changing the inferential target from sorted group averages to the CATE level set itself.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: ML estimates suggest treatment-benefit subgroups -> data-driven selection creates uncertainty and multiplicity -> uniform guarantees are needed -> obtain honest geometry-aware confidence regions for the CATE threshold set

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the inner/outer plug-in confidence set based on quantiles of a local supremum over the estimated boundary band and its coverage proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It delivers the same mathematical object—a confidence region for a function level set—so the transfer problem is precisely to replace the first-stage process by an orthogonal CATE process.

method_exemplars.technique: Port doubly robust uniform CATE-band Gaussian approximation and multiplier critical values to the shrinking threshold neighborhood.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies causal nuisance-robust simultaneous inference, the ingredient missing from generic level-set confidence-region theory.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt sample-splitting and uniform post-selection calibration used for ML-ranked subgroup guarantees.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly handles inference after data-driven treatment-benefit subgroup selection, although for a scalar sorted-effect curve rather than spatial set geometry.

literature_map:
Bonvini, Kennedy, and Keele (2023, arXiv:2306.17464) define the exact weighted CATE-level-set loss and give the plug-in upper rate; their lower theorem carries xi*gamma<=d.
Audibert and Tsybakov (2007, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:0708.2321) prove sharp fast and super-fast classification rates and the key Hölder–margin crossing restriction.
Their Proposition 3.4 implies that xi*gamma>d is not a single homogeneous regime: with strong density, interior crossing requires xi*min(1,gamma)<=1.
Consequently, the smooth transverse subregime xi=1 and gamma>d is potentially nonempty, whereas most nominal super-margin exponent pairs are geometrically empty.
Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2203.00837) derive the two-branch minimax CATE rate via localized fuzzy hypotheses and a higher-order local R-learner.
That CATE converse does not itself yield a margin-calibrated weighted set-loss converse over all measurable set estimators.
Kennedy (2023, arXiv:2004.14497) supplies a doubly robust CATE oracle inequality and local-polynomial estimator, useful for law-level achievability transfer.
Rigollet and Vert (2009, Bernoulli, HAL:hal-00114180) give sharp plug-in density-level-set rates under local smoothness and a margin-like exponent, an adjacent set-estimation analogue.
Reeve, Cannings, and Samworth (2023, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2109.01077) prove minimax regret for low-complexity subgroup selection, but their constrained class and Type-I-error target differ from unrestricted CATE level sets.
Mammen and Polonik (2013, Journal of Multivariate Analysis, DOI:10.1016/j.jmva.2013.07.017) construct generic level-set confidence regions from local supremum quantiles.
Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017, Journal of Applied Econometrics, DOI:10.1002/jae.2574) give doubly robust uniform CATE bands, but not margin-adaptive confidence regions for CATE level sets.
Li and Imai (2023, arXiv:2310.07973) give uniform guarantees for ML-sorted group-average effects, leaving spatial CATE threshold-set coverage as a different inferential object.
